column1: # The original's load-time fix-ups (opence_census::fixups) and how the importer compares: same, differs, replaced or none.

column3: Resolves each call's function by name, as the importer does (Call.function is the name); but it parses string, variable and named constants again from their source text, and fails a script whose non-string constant's written type is not its type ("you need to recompile"). The importer decodes each constant as its written type and keeps a named one's name and index as written; the runtime casts.

A scenario with too many globals or scripts, or a global of no type, has its scripts disabled and still loads; the importer refuses the whole level (the blocks' maxima, value_type's fault). It also grows the string constants by 0x400 for the console, which the engine has no need of. Then hs_compile_postprocess (its own row).

Sets each object name's runtime type and datum from the placements by name index, in object-type order, so the last placement of a name wins; the tool runs it as it builds the map. The importer reads the stored type and datum as object_new_by_name does (Campaign.object_placements), so a name no placement names is the first biped placement, as the tool left it. level::object_names ports the rule, checked against the original by tools/engine_object_names_reference.py, and the stock maps' stored names are the rule's (object_names_reference.rs); a name whose placement has an empty palette entry names none, as object_new_from_scenario makes none of it.

Sets the linear flag of an interface bitmaps group's images, zeroes a sprite group's sequences' first bitmap index and bitmap count, and drops a last sequence with no bitmaps and no sprites; the tool runs it as it builds the map, and the game reads what it stored. The importer reads the groups as stored, and the stock maps hold the fix-up's results (import/tests/bitmap_groups.rs): their sprite sequences have no first index or count, as the engine's particles, weather and contrails take them. The texture cache's upload (bitmap_verify, texture_cache_bitmap_new) is replaced by the importer's own decoding.
